paragraphs: Google Gemma is a family of machine learning language models, trained model weights and parameters, developed by Google. Google says Gemma models are open models that can be customized, fine-tuned in Colab, and run on-device. The family includes core Gemma releases such as Gemma 1, Gemma 2, Gemma 3, and Gemma 4, each with a model card. Google says Gemma 4 was released with text, audio and image input and a context window of up to 256K.

The family also includes core variants and related lines. These are Gemma 3n, DiffusionGemma, FunctionGemma, EmbeddingGemma, PaliGemma, and ShieldGemma, with ShieldGemma 2 and ShieldGemma 1 model cards, and PaliGemma v2 and v1 model cards. Research and tools include RecurrentGemma, DataGemma, Gemma Scope, and Gemma-APS. RecurrentGemma is the Griffin model, and a RecurrentGemma 2B Instruct model is available, around 3.85Gb in size.

Google offers Gemma models through Kaggle, where access can be requested, and through the Google DeepMind recurrentgemma library on GitHub. Google provides guides for running Gemma with frameworks such as LM Studio, Ollama, LiteRT-LM, llama.cpp, MLX, Tunix (Tune-in-JAX), Hugging Face Transformers, Keras, Unsloth, Google Cloud Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, vLLM, and SGLang. Google says Gemma models are compatible with a wide variety of ecosystem tools.

price_limits.summary: Across the 6 versions, input prices run from $0.05 to $0.65 per million tokens and output prices from $0.1 to $0.65. Gemma 3 4B is the cheapest, at $0.05 per million input tokens and $0.1 per million output tokens. Gemma 4 26B A4B has the largest context window, 262,144 tokens.

family_reading.text: Google Gemma spans 6 versions in the OpenRouter catalog, first released 2024-07-13 and newest on 2026-04-03. All 6 publish open weights, and 2 of the 6 support reasoning. Context windows range from 8192 to 262144 tokens. Inputs cover image, text and video, with text output. Prices vary widely: the newest Gemma 4 26B A4B costs $0.09 per million input and $0.3 output, while Gemma 2 27B costs $0.65 on both sides. Output limits also differ, from 2048 tokens up to 235929. The open weights and low entry prices suit self hosting, experimentation and cost sensitive text or image work. Limits sit in reasoning, which only 2 versions offer, and in the older small context and output ceilings. The newest tiers are the cheapest per token, so older versions look costly by comparison.
